meta.basis: 100 synthetic domain validation cases rewritten from public internet research across flood insurance, condo/HOA project eligibility, insurance underwriting inspections, seller disclosure, municipal permit/occupancy, hazard-zone, and local-use rules that can change post-inspection ask quality.
meta.warning: These are internet-researched synthetic cases, not verified customer interviews, legal advice, insurance advice, lending advice, appraisal advice, code advice, or repair estimates.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA SFHA guidance makes flood-zone status and lender flood-insurance timing material to a repair ask.
cases.deal: Conventional buyer; listing says Zone X but lender flood cert returns AE two days before objection deadline.
expectedLeadScope: insurability and premium confirmation before repair demand
expectedPacketSignals: ask for FEMA map/flood cert reconciliation
route to insurance and lender before credit amount
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not lead with a generic moisture credit; first confirm the flood-zone record and insurance impact so the ask addresses closing risk.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA notes federally backed lenders require flood insurance for buildings in Special Flood Hazard Areas.
cases.deal: FHA buyer in Baton Rouge learns the structure may be in Zone A after inspection found grading issues.
findings: seller says no flood insurance carried
expectedPacketSignals: separate lender condition from repair negotiation
request insurance quote before final ask
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Your response should preserve the drainage issue while verifying whether flood insurance is required and affordable for this loan.

cases.sourceBasis: Flood maps and SFHA terms distinguish mapped flood requirement from visible water-entry defects.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a seller credit after inspector notes basement staining in a coastal property.
expectedExclusions: generic coastal fear without map support
expectedPacketSignals: tie request to observed staining and pump status
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the observed basement evidence, but do not imply the home is in a required flood zone until the current determination is verified.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA flood-risk resources warn that flood risk can affect homeowners outside high-risk zones too.
cases.deal: Cash buyer in a creekside subdivision asks for a big credit after heavy rain during inspection.
expectedPacketSignals: distinguish voluntary flood policy from lender mandate
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should focus on documented drainage and water-entry risk, plus insurance due diligence, instead of treating every creekside lot as automatically uninsurable.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA terminology recognizes LOMA determinations as property-specific flood map outcomes.
cases.deal: Listing includes an old LOMA, but lender flood cert still flags the unit in AE.
expectedPacketSignals: request complete LOMA and flood cert comparison
route to lender before demand deadline
include contractor scope only for physical defects
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before asking for a dollar credit, confirm whether the lender will accept the LOMA and separately request repairs for flood vents and equipment support.

cases.sourceBasis: Citizens and wind-mitigation documentation guidance ties Florida insurance credits to permit and roof-code evidence.
cases.deal: Older Tampa home; buyer expected wind-mitigation discounts but roof replacement permit cannot be located.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The negotiation should ask for missing documentation and insurance-condition clarification, not just a cosmetic credit.

cases.sourceBasis: Florida insurance inspections commonly scrutinize roof, electrical, plumbing, and HVAC condition for older homes.
cases.deal: Buyer is within inspection period on a 1978 home and cannot bind coverage until 4-point issues are cleared.
findings: roof at end of service life
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: These are likely insurance gating items; your ask should target coverage approval rather than a broad wish list.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae property-insurance guidance requires acceptable coverage for required perils and may need separate coverage for exclusions.
cases.deal: Coastal condo master policy excludes named windstorm unless separate policy is in force.
expectedPacketSignals: escalate to lender before repair amendment
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not make this only a drywall repair request; the packet needs HOA insurance evidence and responsibility allocation.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae condo master insurance requirements can make deductible and coverage structure relevant to loan eligibility.
cases.deal: Three-unit condo shows a large per-unit wind deductible in the master policy.
findings: master policy deductible appears above lender overlay
roof flashing leak over common stair
expectedExclusions: stained hallway carpet unless active water damage
expectedPacketSignals: ask lender to confirm deductible acceptability
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should protect both repair scope and loan eligibility by confirming deductible and HO-6/loss-assessment coverage.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae requires master policies for many condo projects and individual policies when unit interiors are not covered.
cases.deal: Buyer is purchasing a loft condo where master policy says bare-walls coverage only.
expectedPacketSignals: separate HOA claim scope from buyer HO-6 need
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The repair ask should identify who insures and repairs the damaged improvements before asking the seller for a flat credit.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae project guidance treats projects with critical repairs or deferred maintenance as eligibility risks.
cases.deal: Buyer wants a credit for a unit in a building with scaffolding and a pending facade assessment.
expectedPacketSignals: request HOA minutes and reserve/assessment docs
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This is a building-level risk, so your response should require HOA documentation before narrowing the ask to the unit window.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae ineligible-project guidance identifies condo hotels, transient use, and rental-pooling structures as risks.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to use conventional financing on a resort-branded condo with daily rental desk.
expectedPacketSignals: do not draft only repair request
ask seller for HOA rental and occupancy rules
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The biggest issue is not the noisy AC; confirm whether the project is financeable before spending leverage on minor repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: HUD FHA condo guidance includes insurance, owner occupancy, financial condition, litigation, and physical condition as project factors.
cases.deal: FHA buyer is under contract in a small condo association with no active FHA approval shown.
expectedPacketSignals: request FHA approval or single-unit approval path
avoid assuming seller can fix HOA eligibility
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Your ask should preserve the electrical issue while urgently confirming whether this condo can close under FHA.

cases.sourceBasis: HUD FHA condo review considers pending legal action and project financial condition.
cases.deal: FHA condo buyer learns the HOA is suing the developer over drainage defects.
expectedPacketSignals: request litigation summary and HOA minutes
avoid legal conclusion in buyer message
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This should be framed as document and lender-review contingency risk, not as a simple seller repair list.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae ineligible-project rules identify single-entity ownership and project characteristics that can block conventional financing.
cases.deal: Inspection finds ordinary defects, but resale certificate shows one investor owns 38 percent of units.
findings: pool deck cracking in common area
expectedPacketSignals: ask lender for project eligibility determination
do not over-focus on water heater
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should not let ordinary unit repairs hide a project-eligibility question that may control whether the loan closes.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae master policy rules require replacement-cost settlement rather than unacceptable loss-settlement limits.
cases.deal: Townhome PUD master policy appears actual-cash-value for roofs after hail losses.
expectedPacketSignals: request master declarations and HOA docs
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask needs policy and responsibility clarity before demanding seller-paid roof repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae additional insurance guidance makes excluded or limited required perils a lender concern.
cases.deal: Condo building near the ocean has a master policy with high named-storm limitations.
expectedPacketSignals: separate common-element ask from unit ask
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Treat the coverage limitation as a closing-risk signal and the balcony/slider items as repair evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA lead disclosure rules make pre-1978 lead information a transactional disclosure item, not just a repainting concern.
cases.deal: 1925 rowhome; seller disclosure packet omits lead pamphlet and inspection finds peeling exterior paint.
expectedPacketSignals: do not diagnose lead from photos
warn about family health and repair protocol
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for disclosure completion and safe paint handling; do not frame this as cosmetic repainting.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA radon real estate resources support testing and mitigation decisions during home sale due diligence.
cases.deal: Inspection package includes a short-term radon test above action level; seller offers decorative fixes instead.
expectedLeadScope: sump pit sealing as part of mitigation quote
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A quality ask should prioritize mitigation and retesting rather than accepting unrelated cosmetic concessions.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance underwriting commonly treats knob-and-tube or obsolete electrical conditions as bindability risks.
cases.deal: Buyer cannot get preferred insurance quote for a 1910 bungalow until electrical concerns are resolved.
expectedLeadScope: roof maintenance only if carrier flags it
expectedPacketSignals: ask broker for carrier-specific blocker list
do not imply all old wiring is automatically unsafe
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Tie the request to insurance bindability and licensed electrical evaluation instead of a generic modernization demand.

cases.sourceBasis: HOA and condo master insurance rules require responsibility mapping between unit, common elements, and association policy.
cases.deal: Condo inspection shows ceiling leak below roof; seller says HOA handles it after closing.
expectedLeadScope: escrow/credit path if HOA timing is uncertain
expectedPacketSignals: avoid relying on verbal seller assurance
identify lender concern if active leak remains
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Require written HOA proof or a clear seller remedy; do not accept a verbal promise on an active roof leak.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae project standards can treat deferred common-element repairs as project-level risks.
cases.deal: Buyer loves the unit but inspection notes failing elevated walkway serving multiple units.
expectedLeadScope: common walkway safety and HOA repair plan
expectedPacketSignals: ask HOA for board minutes/reserve study
separate common-element safety from unit appliance issue
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The walkway may affect safety and project review, so it should lead the packet ahead of ordinary unit issues.

cases.sourceBasis: Condo project eligibility can be affected by pending special assessments and inadequate reserves.
cases.deal: HOA disclosed a possible elevator assessment after buyer's inspection objection was drafted.
expectedPacketSignals: do not bury assessment behind outlet repairs
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Your response should ask for current assessment and reserve documents before deciding whether a seller credit is enough.

cases.sourceBasis: HOA governing documents determine whether exterior components are seller, owner, or association responsibility.
cases.deal: Inspection finds rotted trim, but seller says exterior maintenance is covered by HOA dues.
findings: rotted exterior trim at unit front
expectedPacketSignals: avoid assigning responsibility from listing remarks
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should first prove who controls the exterior repair, then request the correct party's remedy.

cases.sourceBasis: Condo insurance and HOA documents can affect whether interior damage is handled by master policy or HO-6 coverage.
cases.deal: Inspector finds old water damage under a common drain stack inside a unit wall.
findings: HOA drain stack serves multiple units
expectedPacketSignals: separate concealed common plumbing from unit finish
avoid demanding seller repair if HOA controls stack
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This packet should identify whether the association controls the drain stack before asking the seller for finish repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae ineligible-project guidance flags short-term rental and hotel-like operations in condo projects.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to live in a downtown condo where many units are advertised nightly online.
expectedPacketSignals: request HOA rules and management agreement
avoid focusing only on detector replacement
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm the project's financing eligibility before treating this as a routine inspection response.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae project standards include litigation and physical condition as relevant project risks.
cases.deal: Buyer asks seller to repair unit defects while HOA litigation over stucco water intrusion is pending.
expectedLeadScope: AC service only after major risk is addressed
expectedPacketSignals: avoid implying seller can settle HOA lawsuit
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The buyer message should request project documents and moisture remediation proof, not just a seller punch list.

cases.sourceBasis: Condo master policy rules make blanket coverage for shared structures a document issue, not an inspector-only issue.
cases.deal: Small self-managed condo cannot produce current master policy declarations before contingency deadline.
expectedPacketSignals: warn lender project review may stall
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Without master policy evidence, the deal has a documentation risk that should lead the inspection response.

cases.sourceBasis: HOA assessment and reserve issues can affect buyer affordability after inspection even when defects are common elements.
cases.deal: Townhome community announces siding replacement assessment after inspector finds siding rot.
findings: seller says dues will cover it
expectedLeadScope: seller concession tied to known assessment if applicable
expectedPacketSignals: ask for board minutes and resale package update
separate common project from unit maintenance
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Get the assessment status in writing before deciding whether to ask for a seller credit or walkaway protection.

cases.sourceBasis: Condo HO-6 needs depend on master-policy interior coverage and lender requirements.
cases.deal: Co-op-style condo unit has upgraded kitchen, but master policy excludes owner improvements.
expectedPacketSignals: do not assume HOA covers upgrades
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should protect the damaged improvement and clarify insurance responsibility before negotiating dollars.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae project rules identify critical repairs and unsafe conditions as project-level concerns.
cases.deal: Balcony inspections after a reserve study show spalling concrete and access restrictions.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid treating balcony closure as cosmetic
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A closed balcony is a safety and project-review issue; the response should demand documents and repair plan clarity.

cases.sourceBasis: HOA rules can determine whether post-inspection repairs are even allowed without architectural approval.
cases.deal: Buyer asks seller to install a new exterior AC condenser pad before closing in a strict HOA.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid asking for unauthorized exterior change
offer credit/escrow alternative if approval lags
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should avoid requiring seller work that the HOA may not approve before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Condo projects with mixed-use or commercial space may require lender review beyond unit inspection defects.
cases.deal: Inspection notes restaurant exhaust odor in a mixed-use condo above retail.
expectedPacketSignals: request condo questionnaire and commercial-space percentage
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should include both the unit defect and a lender check on mixed-use project characteristics.

cases.sourceBasis: HOA master insurance may need ordinance or law coverage for project developments under Fannie Mae rules.
cases.deal: Older converted warehouse condo has high seismic retrofit exposure and unclear ordinance coverage.
findings: master policy ordinance coverage not shown
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not reduce this to a countertop negotiation; confirm insurance and retrofit exposure before final ask.

cases.sourceBasis: Project insurance documents can reveal exclusions that change whether a defect is negotiable with seller or HOA.
cases.deal: HOA says sewer laterals are owner responsibility despite common line backups in disclosures.
expectedPacketSignals: request HOA docs and sewer history
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should define lateral responsibility and obtain a sewer scope before assigning cost to the seller.

cases.sourceBasis: Condo owner-occupancy and project financial condition are part of HUD FHA project considerations.
cases.deal: Buyer wants FHA financing in a condo with many rentals and unpaid HOA dues.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid leading with furnace age alone
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: First confirm FHA project eligibility; otherwise a repair concession may not solve the closing problem.

cases.sourceBasis: Condo master policies must generally cover common elements and residential structures when required.
cases.deal: Self-managed four-unit building says each owner insures only their unit, but common roof is leaking.
expectedPacketSignals: do not accept individual policies as automatic substitute
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should demand insurance and roof responsibility evidence before settling on a seller credit.

cases.sourceBasis: HOA rule violations can affect use and cost after closing even if inspection defects are minor.
cases.deal: Seller enclosed patio without HOA approval; inspector sees water intrusion at enclosure.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid asking buyer to inherit violation
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should require proof the enclosure is legal and approved, plus repair of the water entry.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae ineligible-project guidance includes recreational leases and mandatory memberships as project risks.
cases.deal: Resort condo has mandatory club fees and pool structure defects.
findings: mandatory club membership in HOA packet
expectedPacketSignals: do not frame club fee as inspection repair
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This response should flag project eligibility and cost obligations separately from unit repair items.

cases.sourceBasis: Project-level insurance and maintenance issues can make seller credits insufficient if the association controls the defect.
cases.deal: Buyer asks for credit for common hallway leak entering the unit from exterior masonry.
expectedLeadScope: interior restoration only after source repair
expectedPacketSignals: avoid credit that leaves active source unresolved
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A credit for plaster alone is weak if the common exterior leak remains unresolved.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas Property Code seller disclosure includes flood-zone and prior flood-claim questions that can affect inspection negotiations.
cases.deal: Disclosure checked no flood claims, but inspector sees flood-cut drywall and neighbor reports prior Harvey claim.
findings: seller disclosure says no flood claim
expectedPacketSignals: route to broker/legal channel if discrepancy persists
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should request clarification and documentation on flood history, not simply ask for a cleanup credit.

cases.sourceBasis: California NHD guidance covers statutory hazard zones including flood, dam inundation, high fire, earthquake fault, seismic, and wildland fire areas.
cases.deal: Inspection finds hillside drainage issues before the buyer receives the Natural Hazard Disclosure report.
expectedLeadScope: insurance availability check if fire or seismic zone
expectedPacketSignals: do not finalize ask before NHD if deadline allows
connect visible slope defects to disclosure review
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Wait for the NHD or condition the ask on it; the physical defects may carry larger hazard-zone and insurance implications.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA lead disclosure applies to pre-1978 housing and requires known lead information before contract.
cases.deal: Buyer plans to sand original trim in a 1940 duplex; disclosure package is incomplete.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid saying paint is lead without test
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should focus on disclosure completion and lead-safe handling rather than ordinary repainting.

cases.sourceBasis: EPA radon resources support testing during real estate transactions and mitigation when results warrant.
cases.deal: Seller refuses radon mitigation because radon was not mentioned in the general inspection report.
findings: separate radon report above action level
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Radon should be handled as a separate environmental ask with mitigation and retest documentation.

cases.sourceBasis: New York disclosure reforms and flood-risk disclosure practices make known flood history relevant to buyer due diligence.
cases.deal: Buyer receives property condition disclosure after inspection shows basement flood repairs.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the inspection evidence to request flood-history clarification and a working drainage solution.

cases.sourceBasis: Seller disclosures often distinguish known material defects from inspector estimates, requiring careful wording.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to accuse seller of concealment because attic mold-like staining was painted over.
findings: seller disclosure says no known leaks
expectedExclusions: loose handrail only if not safety-critical
expectedPacketSignals: avoid concealment accusation in generated buyer message
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The message should stay factual: request repair records and ventilation correction without asserting seller intent.

cases.sourceBasis: Federal lead rules apply to sellers, landlords, agents, and property managers in pre-1978 sale or lease transactions.
cases.deal: Seller will lease back for 45 days in a 1955 home with peeling paint.
expectedLeadScope: sale and lease lead disclosure review
expectedPacketSignals: flag both sale and rental disclosure contexts
request broker/legal review for leaseback forms
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Because the seller will rent back, lead disclosure and paint safety should be handled before finalizing the occupancy arrangement.

cases.sourceBasis: Texas seller disclosure form includes prior flood damage, flood insurance, and flood-zone status questions.
cases.deal: Inspection finds drainage defects after seller disclosed previous flood insurance but no prior water penetration.
expectedLeadScope: insurance premium and claim history review
expectedPacketSignals: ask for prior claim/loss history if available
tie request to observed baseboard staining
avoid assuming flood event caused staining
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Your ask should clarify disclosure details and request drainage repair based on visible evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: California hazard disclosures can change insurance availability and buyer risk tolerance after inspection.
cases.deal: Home inspection finds ember-entry vulnerabilities before buyer receives fire-zone disclosure.
findings: wood shake accent siding near vents
expectedPacketSignals: ask for NHD before final concessions
do not promise carrier acceptance after vegetation cleanup
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should combine physical mitigation with insurance confirmation once the fire-zone disclosure is available.

cases.sourceBasis: Disclosure duties for environmental hazards such as lead and radon should not be converted into unsupported diagnoses.
cases.deal: Buyer asks product to demand mold, lead, radon, and asbestos credits from one damp basement photo.
expectedLeadScope: lead disclosure check for pre-1978 home
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should ask for moisture evaluation and relevant disclosures/tests, not assert multiple environmental hazards without evidence.

cases.sourceBasis: Local disclosures can include septic, well, drainage, or private road matters that affect post-inspection asks.
cases.deal: Inspection notes plumbing backups, but seller disclosure did not identify private septic system location.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm whether the home is on septic and request records/testing before deciding on a repair credit.

cases.sourceBasis: Private water sources can require potability and system documentation in rural transactions.
cases.deal: Buyer discovers after inspection that the house uses a shared well with no written agreement.
expectedPacketSignals: separate pump repair from legal access issue
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not make this only a pressure-tank repair; the shared-well agreement may affect financing and future use.

cases.sourceBasis: Local disclosure and permitting records can reveal whether additions are counted as legal living area.
cases.deal: Listing includes converted garage as bedroom, but disclosure is silent and inspector notes no heat or egress.
expectedPacketSignals: request permit records before repair demand
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should require legal-use and safety verification, not just a credit for missing heat.

cases.sourceBasis: Local flood and stormwater disclosures may differ from FEMA map status and still matter to buyers.
cases.deal: Property is outside SFHA but city drainage map shows recurrent street flooding.
expectedLeadScope: insurance quote for optional flood coverage
expectedPacketSignals: distinguish FEMA zone from local drainage evidence
request city drainage records if available
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should address local drainage risk without incorrectly saying flood insurance is federally required.

cases.sourceBasis: Municipal or state disclosure forms can require known unpermitted work or code orders to be disclosed.
cases.deal: Seller disclosure says no known permits open, but township portal shows final inspection missing for deck.
findings: deck permit open with no final
expectedPacketSignals: request seller close permit before closing
avoid asking buyer to inherit code issue
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should require permit closure and safety repair documentation, not just a price concession.

cases.sourceBasis: Municipal certificate-of-occupancy programs require completed permit inspections before legal occupancy in some jurisdictions.
cases.deal: Portland addition has permits issued but no final inspection or certificate of occupancy documentation.
expectedPacketSignals: condition seller remedy on final approval
avoid assuming as-built approval is easy
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not accept cosmetic completion as proof; require municipal final approval or a clear risk allocation.

cases.sourceBasis: Local building permits are commonly required for structural, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and egress-altering work.
cases.deal: Basement finish appears recent, but county permit search shows no record.
expectedPacketSignals: do not call room a legal bedroom without proof
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should prioritize legal occupancy and safety rather than treating the basement as finished living area by default.

cases.sourceBasis: Open permits can create municipal, insurance, and resale friction after closing.
cases.deal: Roof replacement permit remains open two years after installation, affecting wind-mitigation credit.
findings: wind mitigation cannot verify code year
expectedPacketSignals: request finaled permit or contractor affidavit
avoid assuming roof condition equals code compliance
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask the seller to close the roof permit and provide documentation so insurance underwriting can rely on the roof date.

cases.sourceBasis: Unpermitted electrical panel work can affect safety, insurance, and municipal compliance.
cases.deal: Seller upgraded panel but cannot provide permit; inspection finds mixed workmanship.
findings: new 200 amp panel no permit found
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should require permitted or licensed electrical resolution, not a generic seller credit.

cases.sourceBasis: Municipal final approvals can matter when a seller markets extra bedrooms or baths created by remodel.
cases.deal: Listing says 4 bedrooms, but one is an attic conversion with no permit record.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid using unverified bedroom in ask math
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Base the response on legal-use uncertainty and safety conditions, not only on repair cost.

cases.sourceBasis: Local ordinances can regulate short-term rental occupancy and licensing independent of physical inspection condition.
cases.deal: Buyer intends short-term rentals, but local ordinance requires disclosure of legal STR status.
expectedPacketSignals: route use issue to broker/legal review
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: If rental legality is central to your purchase, confirm STR rights before negotiating minor inspection items.

cases.sourceBasis: Municipal code orders or notices can survive closing and change the value of an inspection ask.
cases.deal: Inspector sees city violation sticker for missing rental license in a duplex bought as owner-occupied with tenant.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should require resolution of the municipal notice before focusing on ordinary unit repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Permit records can conflict with seller statements and should be clarified without alleging intent.
cases.deal: Seller says pool is permitted, but city portal shows final inspection failed.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should require pool permit closure and safety corrections, not a simple pool-service credit.

cases.sourceBasis: Certificates of occupancy or lawful-use records can matter when a multi-unit property is marketed as more units than allowed.
cases.deal: Buyer contracts for a three-family, but city records show legal two-family use.
expectedPacketSignals: do not count illegal rent in buyer value
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This is a lawful-use issue; confirm the legal unit count before negotiating ordinary repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Permit and occupancy rules can affect whether post-closing repairs must be opened to municipal inspection.
cases.deal: Seller offers credit for unpermitted kitchen remodel, but buyer's lender questions appraiser notes.
expectedPacketSignals: warn credit may not cure lender concern
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A credit alone may not solve unpermitted gas/electrical work if the lender or city requires correction.

cases.sourceBasis: Local septic permits and health department records can affect whether a property can support advertised bedroom count.
cases.deal: Listing says five bedrooms, but septic permit on county file is for three bedrooms.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid using advertised bedroom count as verified
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should address septic capacity and legal bedroom count before negotiating basement finish defects.

cases.sourceBasis: Municipal permits can be required for HVAC replacement and may affect insurance or resale documentation.
cases.deal: AC unit is new but no permit or startup documentation is available.
findings: new HVAC condenser no permit found
expectedPacketSignals: avoid demanding replacement of new unit without defect basis
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for installation documentation and targeted corrections rather than assuming a new system is acceptable.

cases.sourceBasis: Unfinaled plumbing permits can leave concealed work unverified by local authority.
cases.deal: Seller completed bathroom addition under permit but never got final inspection.
expectedPacketSignals: ask for licensed corrections before final
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Because the permit is open and defects are visible, the ask should require finaled corrections, not just repair receipts.

cases.sourceBasis: Legal occupancy rules can affect use of accessory dwelling units and rental income after closing.
cases.deal: Buyer values detached studio as ADU, but inspector sees noncompliant utilities and no permit packet.
expectedPacketSignals: request ADU permits and certificate documents
avoid valuing unit as legal rental without proof
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should condition the ask on legal ADU status and safe utilities, not just studio cosmetic repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Municipal records can identify open code enforcement cases that are more urgent than routine inspection defects.
cases.deal: Inspection finds boarded garage window; city portal shows active nuisance/code case.
findings: active code case for garage exterior
expectedPacketSignals: request compliance letter or case closure
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should require closure of the code case or a clear written resolution before closing.

cases.sourceBasis: Permit requirements and floodplain development rules can affect repairs in mapped flood areas.
cases.deal: Home in floodplain has unpermitted ground-level enclosure used as living space.
expectedPacketSignals: do not treat enclosure as legal living area
ask seller for permits and elevation info
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should focus on floodplain compliance and legal use, not a cosmetic flooring credit.

cases.sourceBasis: Pool barrier and permit issues can create insurance liability and municipal compliance risk.
cases.deal: Inspection finds pool fence gaps and city record shows pool resurfacing permit still open.
findings: pool barrier gaps exceed safe practice
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Prioritize legal and safety closure for the pool before negotiating optional amenities.

cases.sourceBasis: Local building records can determine whether a detached structure is permitted for habitation.
cases.deal: Seller markets detached garage apartment, but inspector finds no kitchen permit and questionable stairs.
expectedPacketSignals: separate safety repairs from use approval
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should verify whether the apartment is legal before using it to justify price or repair demands.

cases.sourceBasis: Open permits can delay closing if lender, title, or local transfer practices require closure.
cases.deal: Buyer asks seller to close all permits after inspection finds old open water-heater permit.
findings: open water-heater permit from prior owner
expectedPacketSignals: avoid demanding unrelated municipal search remedies
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: A precise ask should require permit closure and safety corrections for the water heater.

cases.sourceBasis: Local occupancy and fire-safety rules can apply to rental property transfers and post-closing use.
cases.deal: Buyer is purchasing a three-decker with tenants and missing smoke/CO compliance certificate.
findings: smoke detectors missing in common stair
CO detectors absent near sleeping areas
expectedExclusions: peeling porch paint unless lead/safety issue
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should lead with required life-safety compliance, especially because tenants already occupy the property.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA SFHA and flood insurance rules affect financing and buyer cost beyond visible repair items.
cases.deal: Inspection on river-adjacent home finds HVAC below base flood elevation shown on elevation certificate.
expectedPacketSignals: request current elevation certificate and insurance quote
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should account for flood compliance and insurance cost, not merely request a screen repair.

cases.sourceBasis: California NHD fire and seismic zones can influence insurance availability and mitigation asks.
cases.deal: Home in foothills has inspection findings that overlap with wildfire defensible-space concerns.
expectedExclusions: single-pane windows unless tied to required mitigation
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Ask for targeted fire-risk mitigation and insurance confirmation rather than a generic upgrade request.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA flood resources note that flood risk and flood insurance need clear zone classification evidence.
cases.deal: Seller says flood insurance is unnecessary, but detached garage and driveway are in mapped floodplain.
expectedPacketSignals: distinguish main structure from accessory structure
avoid saying entire property requires flood policy
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Clarify which structures are in the flood zone before making insurance or repair demands.

cases.sourceBasis: Natural hazard disclosures can include dam-inundation and seismic zones that are not visible in a general inspection.
cases.deal: NHD shows dam inundation and seismic hazard zones after inspection found foundation cracks.
expectedPacketSignals: tie visible cracks to structural review, not dam speculation
include hazard disclosure in buyer decision packet
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the NHD as risk context, but ground the repair ask in engineer review of the observed foundation movement.

cases.sourceBasis: Flood insurance requirements apply to buildings in SFHAs and should be separated from general water-management repairs.
cases.deal: Appraisal notes Zone AE while inspection only found minor crawlspace humidity.
expectedLeadScope: flood insurance quote and lender clearance
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should not confuse flood insurance with crawlspace humidity; both need separate resolution.

cases.sourceBasis: Hazard-zone and insurance issues can make availability of coverage more important than repair estimates.
cases.deal: Carrier declines quote due to roof debris and wildfire score after inspection.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid claiming code violation without source
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Use the insurer's objections to shape a targeted mitigation ask before negotiating decorative items.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA map terminology distinguishes high-risk A/V zones from lower-risk X zones and Zone D uncertainty.
cases.deal: Property in Zone D has arroyo drainage concerns and no lender flood requirement yet.
expectedPacketSignals: do not call Zone D an SFHA mandate
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Frame Zone D as uncertainty plus observed erosion, not as automatic mandatory flood insurance.

cases.sourceBasis: Coastal wind and flood risks can require different insurance documents and repair evidence.
cases.deal: Buyer conflates flood, wind, and HOA master policy after balcony leak inspection.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should separate insurance categories and unit/common repair responsibility before asking for money.

cases.sourceBasis: Earthquake and seismic disclosures can affect buyer mitigation choices without replacing structural inspection evidence.
cases.deal: NHD shows earthquake fault zone; inspector notes cripple-wall bracing absent.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid stating home is unsafe solely from NHD
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The best ask is a retrofit evaluation and cost discussion, not panic language about the hazard zone alone.

cases.sourceBasis: Flood history and insurance claims are distinct from routine drainage repair, but both can affect buyer risk.
cases.deal: Disclosure says prior flood claim, inspection finds current drainage defect.
expectedLeadScope: insurance quote under current risk profile
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should use the disclosed claim to request documentation and current drainage correction.

cases.sourceBasis: Hazard-zone disclosures may reveal fire or flood risk that makes deferred exterior maintenance more consequential.
cases.deal: Mountain home shows wildfire map risk and inspection finds combustible deck storage.
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Prioritize insurance bindability and deck safety before minor interior trim asks.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA flood maps and local drainage evidence can conflict, requiring careful non-overstated buyer messaging.
cases.deal: Home is outside FEMA SFHA but neighborhood has repeated street flooding reports.
expectedPacketSignals: do not claim mandatory flood insurance
separate public reports from seller knowledge
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should rely on visible drainage/foundation evidence and optional insurance due diligence, not overstate FEMA status.

cases.sourceBasis: Fannie Mae additional insurance rules can require attention to perils excluded from required coverage.
cases.deal: Condo master policy excludes earth movement while inspection finds retaining wall distress.
expectedPacketSignals: avoid saying exclusion makes loan impossible without lender
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The packet should combine engineer review with insurance and HOA responsibility checks.

cases.sourceBasis: FEMA SFHA designations and flood insurance costs can change buyer affordability after inspection.
cases.deal: Buyer discovers required flood policy premium may exceed budget after inspection found little physical damage.
expectedPacketSignals: do not manufacture repair credit from premium alone
ask seller for documented flood mitigation items if present
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: This is primarily an affordability and insurance requirement issue; repair asks should stay tied to actual defects.

cases.sourceBasis: Hazard-zone status can affect lender, insurance, and disclosure review even when seller offers repairs.
cases.deal: Seller offers to fix basement seepage, but FEMA map update may move the house into SFHA before closing.
findings: pending FEMA map update noted by town
expectedPacketSignals: do not rely only on seller repair offer
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm map timing and insurance impact while separately requesting a durable seepage remedy.

cases.sourceBasis: Occupancy limits and legal bedroom count can affect valuation, appraisal, insurance, and safe use after inspection.
cases.deal: Listing advertises six bedrooms, but two basement rooms lack egress and permits.
expectedPacketSignals: do not label rooms bedrooms without legal support
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should protect against overpaying for illegal bedrooms and require life-safety corrections.

cases.sourceBasis: Short-term rental ordinances can determine whether buyer's planned occupancy/use is lawful independent of inspection defects.
cases.deal: Buyer wants to Airbnb a NYC apartment, but local registration law and building rules may block use.
expectedLeadScope: bath fan repair only if buyer proceeds
expectedPacketSignals: do not draft only repair request
route use issue to broker/legal review
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Confirm whether the planned rental use is legal before negotiating ordinary inspection repairs.

cases.sourceBasis: Owner-occupancy and rental restrictions in HOA documents can affect buyer plans and loan eligibility.
cases.deal: Buyer intends to rent immediately, but HOA requires one year owner occupancy before leasing.
findings: unit water heater at end of life
expectedPacketSignals: surface use restriction before repair amount
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should first address whether your intended rental use is allowed, then negotiate actual defects.

cases.sourceBasis: Post-closing occupancy arrangements can create insurance and safety issues when inspection finds material hazards.
cases.deal: Seller rent-back is planned, but inspection finds unsafe gas appliances and missing CO alarms.
expectedLeadScope: gas appliance safety correction before occupancy
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Do not allow an occupancy agreement to outrun life-safety repairs; require clearance before rent-back begins.

cases.sourceBasis: Local rental licensing requirements can affect whether a buyer can continue tenant occupancy after closing.
cases.deal: Buyer assumes existing tenants can stay, but city rental license inspection is overdue.
expectedPacketSignals: request license status and inspection requirements
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should require rental compliance and safety corrections so tenant occupancy does not become an immediate violation.

cases.sourceBasis: Accessory dwelling or guest-house occupancy may require local approval and separate utility safety review.
cases.deal: Buyer needs in-law suite occupancy, but guest house has unpermitted kitchen and unsafe wiring.
findings: guest house kitchen no permit evidence
expectedPacketSignals: avoid assuming family occupancy is exempt
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Verify lawful and safe occupancy for the guest house before relying on it for family housing.

cases.sourceBasis: Senior, assisted, or group occupancy uses may trigger local rules beyond normal single-family inspection scope.
cases.deal: Buyer plans licensed care use in a single-family home with inspection safety defects.
findings: seller markets as perfect group home
expectedPacketSignals: flag use approval outside inspection scope
do not draft as guaranteed group-home approval
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Your planned use needs zoning/licensing confirmation; inspection repairs alone cannot make the property approved for care use.

cases.sourceBasis: Occupancy certificates and lawful-use records can determine whether a basement apartment is financeable and rentable.
cases.deal: Buyer's affordability depends on basement apartment rent, but CO shows single-family only.
expectedPacketSignals: route to lender before repair ask
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The ask should protect you from relying on rent that may not be legal or usable for underwriting.

cases.sourceBasis: Insurance policies can treat vacant or unoccupied properties differently, making utility and safety conditions material before closing.
cases.deal: House has been vacant all winter; buyer wants seller to fix minor items but insurance asks occupancy/vacancy questions.
expectedPacketSignals: turn utilities on before final ask
avoid accepting cosmetic credit before testing systems
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: The response should require active system testing and insurance clarity because vacancy can hide material defects.

cases.sourceBasis: Occupancy restrictions, HOA rules, and insurance underwriting can intersect when a buyer plans non-owner or mixed use.
cases.deal: Buyer plans seasonal rental of a condo, but HOA limits occupancy and insurer asks for rental frequency.
expectedPacketSignals: surface use restriction and insurance classification first
cases.expectedBuyerMessage: Before negotiating minor fixes, confirm that your intended rental pattern is allowed and insurable.
